title: Driver station
summary: DS laptop, Ethernet vs Wi-Fi, firewall, joysticks.

start.question: What is wrong at the driver station?

options.label: DS will not connect to the robot in the pit
DS is red on the field, no FMS
Comms flicker or ping is high
Laptop is slow, sleeps, or updates
DS software will not open or shows a firewall warning

pit-link.question: How is the DS connected to the robot?

pit-ethernet.title: Ethernet in the pit
steps: Plug the cable into the radio DS port. Check link lights on the laptop and the radio.
Turn the laptop Wi-Fi off. Disable every other adapter in ncpa.cpl. Set the Ethernet adapter to DHCP.
Check the team number in the DS Setup tab.
Turn off the Windows firewall, all three profiles.
Ping 10.TE.AM.2. A reply with the DS still red means the DS software, not the network. Restart the DS.

steps.text: Is the DS still not connecting?
steps.yes: Swap the cable or use a USB Ethernet adapter.

pit-wifi.title: Wi-Fi in the pit
steps: Check whether 2.4 GHz pit Wi-Fi is on at this event. Many events turn it off.
The network name is the team number plus the suffix set at the kiosk. The password is the team's 2.4 GHz key.
Unplug Ethernet while on Wi-Fi. Two adapters on the robot network break mDNS.
Check the team number in the DS Setup tab and turn off the firewall.

steps.text: Is the DS still not connecting on Wi-Fi?
steps.yes: Use an Ethernet cable to the radio DS port.

field-ds.title: DS red on the field
steps: Check Enet Link in the Diagnostics tab. Off means the field cable or the laptop port. Reseat both ends. Try the spare cable.
Turn Wi-Fi off with the hardware switch. Disable other adapters. Set Ethernet to DHCP.
Check the team number in the Setup tab matches this match.
Turn off the Windows firewall. Run ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew.
Close and reopen the DS software. Only one copy.

steps.text: Is the DS still red on the field?

latency.title: Comms flicker or high trip time
steps: Check the RIO CPU in the Diagnostics tab. Near 100 percent starves the DS packets. Use the Code and deploy guide, CPU branch.
Check the DS log for bandwidth. Over 4 Mbps means a camera stream is too big. Lower the resolution or frame rate.
Close any dashboard, browser, or camera viewer not needed in the match.
Check the laptop is on Best Performance and plugged in.
Move the radio to the top of the robot. Metal or motors near it hurt the link.

steps.text: Do comms still flicker or trip time stay high?

steps: Pull the match logs. Check whether other robots in the same match also had high trip time or dropped packets.

steps.text: Did the whole field see it, or an outside source?
steps.yes: It is the field or RF environment, not this laptop.
steps.no: Keep working this robot: CPU, bandwidth, radio placement.

joysticks.title: Joysticks not working
steps: Press F1 to rescan. Every controller in the USB tab should be green.
Drag each controller into the slot the code expects. Lock the order so it survives a rescan.
Unplug and replug. Try a laptop port instead of a hub. Use a powered hub if a hub is needed.
Move a stick and watch the axis bars in the USB tab. No movement means the controller, not the code.

steps.text: Is the controller still not working?
steps.yes: Swap the controller. Worn cables drop under vibration.

laptop.title: Laptop settings for competition
steps: Set sleep to Never for plugged in and on battery. Set the power mode to Best Performance.
Pause Windows Update for the event. Do not let it install during a match.
Close everything except the DS and the dashboard. Uninstall third-party antivirus.
Bring the charger to the field and plug in at the station.

steps.text: Is the laptop still too slow to run the DS?

firewall.title: Firewall or DS software problems
steps: Open wf.msc and turn off the Domain, Private, and Public profiles.
Add rules to allow the DS and mDNS if the school locks the firewall. Otherwise use a loaner laptop.
Remove third-party antivirus that adds its own firewall.
Reinstall NI FRC Game Tools for this season if the DS will not open. Run as administrator once.
